problem: Tommy drinks $5$ milliliters of vitamin syrup each day from a bottle. What differential equation describes the rate of change of the amount of vitamin syrup $S$ (in milliliters) remaining in the bottle? Assume that the time $t$ is measured in days.

feedback.worked_solution:
If the number of copies remaining in stock is $N,$ then the rate of change of the number of copies is $\frac{\text{d}N}{\text{d}t},$ where $t$ is the time in days.

Since $27$ copies are sold each day, the rate of change of the number of copies is given by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}N}{\text{d}t}=-27.
$$

The right-hand side is negative because the number of copies remaining is *decreasing*.
